items.title: The Great Missionary Hope
items.summary: God’s call is irresistible in the sense that it can overcome all resistance. It is infallibly effective according to God’s purpose.

items.title: Christ Is Like Sunlight
items.summary: We see the sun by means of seeing the rays of the sun. So also we see God the Father by seeing Jesus.

items.title: God’s Final, Decisive Word
items.summary: The Word that God spoke by his Son is the decisive Word. It will not be followed in this age by any greater word or replacement word.

items.title: Hedonism for Husbands and Wives
items.summary: When Christ redeems marriage, he does not dismantle loving headship and willing submission. He restores it.

items.title: The Mystery of Marriage
items.summary: Husbands and wives should seek to live after the distinctive model of God’s pure and glad design for Christ and the church.

items.title: Prayer’s First Priority
items.summary: The first priority in praying is to ask our heavenly Father to cause his name to be hallowed. In us. In the church. In the world. Everywhere.

items.title: Love’s Greatest Happiness
items.summary: The union between Christ and his bride is so close that any good done to her is a good done to himself.

items.title: When God Is Against Me
items.summary: Can God act as a Christian’s enemy through suffering? Pastor John explains how God’s painful providences do not conflict with his enduring love for his children.

items.title: Can My Pain Kill My Sins?
items.summary: Does suffering kill the sin within us? Pastor John argues from 1 Peter 4:1 that believers die to sin with Christ so we can live to his righteousness.

items.title: Trapped in a Meaningless Life
items.summary: Loss can lead to despair over God’s plan for our lives. When we can’t perceive meaning in life, Pastor John counsels us to find comfort in God’s glorious purpose in Christ.

items.title: Do Good People Get Hurt?
items.summary: Does the Bible promise that believers will not be harmed for doing good? Pastor John explains the context of 1 Peter 3:13 and God’s sovereign wisdom in suffering.

items.title: The Marriage Miracle That Takes Time
items.summary: Loving our spouses for better or worse includes loving them through their spiritual apathy. Pastor John gives ten encouragements for the weary.

items.title: When You’re Not Sorry
items.summary: When someone confronts you wrongly, should you apologize? Pastor John encourages humility and reconciliation without giving in to emotional manipulation.

items.title: Love and the Future of God
items.summary: We’ve been looking at the ways in which an experience of the grace of God creates a new interior character of the heart. At the end of 1 Corinthians 13, Paul tells us that the secret, the key, to developing that interior supernaturally changed heart is to look to the future—to something that’s going to happen in the…

items.title: The Keller Family discusses The Global Reach Project
items.summary: Gospel in Life recently launched The Global Reach Project (https://theglobalreachproject.com), which is an initiative to translate 500 of Tim Keller’s most foundational sermons into 30 of the world’s most spoken languages. This project is something Kathy Keller and her family are truly excited about, and we brought…

items.title: Living Grace
items.summary: Long before Marx, Nietzsche, and Foucault rightly noticed that normally people follow moral virtue out of fear, pride, and a desire for power, the apostle Paul said it’s extremely possible to live a completely ethical life without any love at the root of it. We’re looking at the traits that show not just moral…

items.title: Enduring Grace
items.summary: In the last 40 years or so, we’ve had an explosion of 12-step groups helping people with a range of addictions. And even if you don’t have those addictions, think of how much misery there is in our lives because we can’t control our tongue or our time or our thoughts. Just about everybody has a problem with…

items.title: Passionate Grace
items.summary: A lot of people think that to say Christians have a changed relationship to the truth means that Christians become honest. It’s not less than that. Technical, ethical honesty is one thing. But we’re talking about something more and deeper. In Ephesians 4:15, Paul says, “speaking the truth in love.” But what Paul…

items.title: Blessed Self-Forgetfulness
items.summary: To talk about humility means we’re getting into a very culturally interesting subject, which is self-esteem. Traditional cultures have believed that having too high a view of yourself is the real root cause for most of the evil in the world. But in modern Western culture, particularly in the United States, we have an…

items.title: Near the Brokenhearted
items.summary: The good life is not the absence of hardship. It is the nearness of the Lord in the middle of it.

items.title: Saved by Grace
items.summary: Our own strength isn't sufficient to save us. Through Christ alone, we find hope and a settled peace.

items.title: They Had Been With Jesus
items.summary: Spending time with Jesus transforms you, His presence becoming visible to those around you.

items.title: The Gift of Friends
items.summary: Faithful friendship is centered on Christ, grounded in love, and always pointing each other back to Him.

items.title: The Strength of Companions
items.summary: Walking with like-minded believers provides us with counsel and support to do great things for the Lord.

items.title: A Beloved Brother
items.summary: Because of Christ's sacrifice, we are no longer slaves to sin but are welcomed into the family of God.

items.title: The Reward of the Believer
items.summary: Our prize isn't something we earn through performance—it's the joy of living a life rooted in Christ.

items.title: Trust Amid Uncertainty (2 Chronicles 20:12)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 20:12, David Platt calls us to trust God when we don’t know what to do. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Leading People Back to God (2 Chronicles 19:4)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 19:4, David Platt invites us into God’s restorative work through love, prayer, and witness. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Faithfulness to Speak God's Word (2 Chronicles 18:13)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 18:13, David Platt prays for each follower of Jesus to faithfully speak God’s Word, regardless of the cost. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Courage To Persevere (2 Chronicles 15:7)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 15:7, David Platt exhorts us to work wholeheartedly for God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Relying on God Through Prayer (2 Chronicles 14:11)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 14:11, David Platt reminds us that God is the ultimate source of strength for believers. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Guard Your Heart (2 Chronicles 12:14)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 12:14, David Platt reminds us to avoid evil by seeking God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Blessed for God's Own Glory (2 Chronicles 9:8)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 9:8, David Platt reminds us that God blesses his people for his own glory among the nations. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: God’s Love Begins With Him, Not You
items.summary: God’s love is not something we earn through our obedience, nor is it an excuse to continue in sin. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how God’s love flows from His character, is revealed through Jesus Christ, and transforms how we love others. Resources: In Jesus' Name I Pray: TJ the Squirrel Learns the True Heart…

items.title: When God’s Glory Exposes Your Sin
items.summary: We are often quick to recognize the sins of others while overlooking our own. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how seeing God in His holiness strips away our excuses, exposes our sin, and calls us to genuine repentance.

items.title: You Can Know God But Never Master Him
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be incomprehensible. God is infinitely greater than our minds can comprehend, yet He has made Himself truly knowable through His Word and ultimately through Jesus Christ.

items.title: Your View of God Shapes Everything
items.summary: You may not deny God, but do you diminish Him? In this episode, Costi Hinn examines how a small or distorted view of God can shape the way we live, exposing the gap between what we confess about God and how we actually function day to day.

items.title: No One Is Above God
items.summary: The name El Elyon means “God Most High,” declaring God’s absolute supremacy over everyone and everything. In this final episode of the Names of God series, Costi Hinn explains what it means to live with the perspective that God is sovereign, owns everything, and answers to no one.
